data.title: LINP1 suppresses radiation-induced cellular senescence in keratinocytes by modulating the mTOR-p53 axis
data.authors: Liang X; Hou M; Liu Yaru; Yang Y; Zhang C; Zhang Z; Zhou L

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Human keratinocytes; ex vivo human skin explants
data.finding: LncRNA LINP1 binds the FAT domain of mTOR, reduces mTOR-p53 interaction and p53 Ser15 phosphorylation, thereby suppressing radiation-induced cellular senescence in keratinocytes and human skin.
data.abstract_excerpt: LINP1 is a markedly upregulated lncRNA following ionizing radiation (IR). LINP1 promotes cell survival and limits radiation-induced DNA damage accumulation. Mechanistically, LINP1 attenuates radiation-induced cellular senescence through modulation of the mTOR-p53 signaling axis: LINP1 associates with the FAT domain of mTOR, attenuates the interaction between mTOR and p53, thereby reducing p53 Ser15 phosphorylation and downstream senescence-associated signaling.

extracted_findings.target: mTOR FAT domain; mTOR-p53 interaction; p53 Ser15 phosphorylation; cellular senescence
extracted_findings.effect: LINP1 directly binds mTOR FAT domain to reduce mTOR-p53 interaction, decrease p53 activation, and suppress radiation-induced senescence
